title: kv-cache: adaptive defrag + spillover paging scheduler and eviction priority improvements
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context and motivation: The KV cache has seen increased fragmentation and memory pressure on high-concurrency workloads, leading to unbounded heap growth in rare tail cases and degraded token throughput due to synchronous spill-to-host operations. This PR implements a coordinated set of runtime changes to improve memory management: an adaptive in-place defragmentation pass, a background spillover paging scheduler that batches/serializes host IO to avoid blocking inference threads, and an eviction-priority refinement that better accounts for fragment size and recent access patterns.

Summary of changes: - Add a concurrent adaptive defragmentation worker that merges adjacent free segments and compacts small fragments when memory pressure crosses a configurable threshold. The worker runs on a low-priority runtime thread and yields to inference work; defrag window and target compaction ratio are tunable via kv_cache.defrag.* flags. - Implement spillover paging to host SSD using a batched I/O path: cold KV segments are paged out asynchronously into a compact on-disk format; the loader is integrated with request scheduling so hot segments are prioritized for prefetch. - Introduce an eviction priority score that combines LRU recency, segment fragmentation penalty, and estimated rehydration cost; this reduces unnecessary rehydrates for large fragmented segments. - Background scheduler: a work-queue-based scheduler orchestrates defrag, spillout, and prefetch tasks, enforcing a global IO budget and accounting for current GPU utilization to avoid interfering with low-latency paths. - Kernel/allocator changes: improved alignment for KV blobs to reduce fragmentation, and a small allocator rewrite to prefer large contiguous allocations when fragmentation is high. - Observability: new metrics (kv.defrag.{runs,bytes_compacted}, kv.spill.{scheduled,completed}, kv.eviction.{score_histogram}) and corresponding dashboards.

Files touched (high level): - runtime/kv_cache/defrag_worker.cc (+420/-33): core defrag and worker loop. - runtime/kv_cache/spill_pager.cc (+310/-18): paging format, batched IO. - runtime/kv_cache/eviction_policy.h (+45/-6): eviction score and priority comparator. - runtime/kv_cache/allocator.cc (+210/-120): allocator heuristics and alignment changes. - runtime/scheduler/kv_background_scheduler.cc (+120/-4): integrates with global scheduler and IO budget. - observability/metrics/kv_cache_prometheus.yaml (+40/-0): adds metrics. - tests/kv_cache/defrag_integration_test.cc (+90/-0): new integration tests. - docs/notes/kv-cache-defrag-spillover.md (+18/-0): design notes and flags.

Commits summary: [a3b1f2d] initial defrag worker and allocator hooks; [b4c2e7a] spill pager v1 with batched IO format; [c5d3f9b] eviction score and tests; [d6e4a1f] scheduler integration and IO budgeting; [e7f5b2c] metrics + dashboards + docs; [f8a6c3d] followups: tunable defaults and benchmark numbers.

Behavioral compatibility and migration: Default behavior is conservative and feature-gated via runtime flags (kv_cache.defrag.enabled, kv_cache.spill.enabled, kv_cache.eviction.adaptive=true). When disabled, existing allocations and eviction logic remain unchanged. The on-disk spill format includes a version header to allow safe roll-forward; we also added a guard so older workers won't attempt to load pages written with newer schema.

Benchmarks & results: Microbenchmarks on p3.2xlarge testbed with max-concurrency=512 and synthetic long-context workloads: - Mean mem-usage during steady-state reduced by ~28% (before: 37GB, after: 27GB) - 95th percentile per-request latency improved by 12% under high memory-pressure scenarios - Cold-start rehydrate cost reduced by 34% due to batched prefetching - End-to-end token throughput improved by ~8% for batch sizes <= 8. See docs/notes/kv-cache-defrag-spillover.md for full tables and graphs.

Testing: Unit tests for eviction scoring, allocator invariants, and spill formats. Integration tests simulate fragmentation patterns and verify correctness of defrag (no missing keys) and that spill files round-trip. Added stress runs in perf-canary harness; CI runs include a durability matrix for mixed old/new workers.

Rollout plan: - Feature gated off by default in hosted for first canary wave. - Canary rollout to Dedicated pools with opt-in flags and increased logging. - Monitor kv.defrag.* and kv.spill.* metrics and series of alerts for increased rehydrates or IO backlog. - Gradual enablement after 2 weeks of stable telemetry.

Related: ENG-4521 tracks long-term allocator redesign; SUP-3271 incident postmortem referenced memory growth observed on 2024-09-27.

Notes: This PR trades some background IO for reduced peak memory usage and fewer synchronous rehydrates. Tunables are conservative; follow-up PR planned to add adaptive thresholds driven by observed working set characteristics.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez (reviewer): Can we bound the max IO bandwidth the background scheduler can consume? We saw spikes in CI when the pager ran concurrently with heavy inference. -- Asha: Added a global io_budget config and integrated with scheduler; default is 100MB/s and we throttle per-pool.

Maya Chen (reviewer): Eviction score looks promising but we should avoid oscillation when recency flips quickly. Suggest hysteresis or cooldown on resurrected segments. -- Asha: Added a cooldown window and unit tests verifying non-oscillation.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Consider exposing some of these tunables via the console for Dedicated customers. -- Asha: Filed ENG-4590 for console exposure; left flags runtime-only for hosted GA.
Maya Chen: Add more logging around spilled file version and rehydrate latency for initial canaries. -- Asha: Added version header and rehydrate latency histogram metrics.
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory management: adaptive defragmentation, asynchronous spillover paging, and refined eviction priority to reduce memory pressure and tail latency. Feature-gated and disabled by default; rollout planned as canary then gradual enablement.
notes: Follow-up work: telemetry-driven adaptive thresholds, console tunables (ENG-4590), and an optional SSD caching tier for Dedicated customers.
